newsitem.title: CUBA: Australian postpones Cuba-U.S. swim start.
newsitem.headline: Australian postpones Cuba-U.S. swim start.

text.p: Australian marathon swimmer Susie Maroney on Friday postponed the start of a second attempt to swim from Cuba to the United States to wait for better weather, a member of her support team said.

The start of the swim, originally planned for early Friday, could now take place on Monday or Tuesday. "It depends on what the weather does," the aide told Reuters from the team's base at a Havana hotel.

Only a light breeze ruffled the sea off Havana on Friday, but the 22-year-old Australian swimmer has said she would prefer flat, calm conditions to attempt the 58-mile (93 km) distance from Cuba to Key West.
In her first attempt last year, Maroney was battered by a storm and unexpected currents and was plucked from the water 12 miles (19 km) short of the Florida Keys after 38 hours and 30 minutes.
This year, her navigation team will be using satellite photographs to try to plot the best course through the shifting currents of the Gulf Stream.
